descriptor: Defence electronics and missile subsystems maker moving into explosives and weapon systems
lede: Apollo Micro Systems makes guidance, control and fuzing electronics for Indian missile, torpedo and naval programmes and is buying into explosives. Q2 FY27 revenue was a record ₹388 Cr (+72%) and standalone margin 35%, but standalone H1 growth of 29% is below the 40% guided, operating cash flow has been negative for years, the big MIGM order is still to come, and the stock trades near 113x earnings.

short_version.text: Record Q2: consolidated revenue +72%, EBITDA ₹111 Cr (29% margin), standalone margin 35%. Order book ₹1,765 Cr, MIGM order called certain this financial year and would lift it to ₹4,500-5,000 Cr; new Unit 3 capacity and a CCI-cleared Premier deal.

Standalone growth is only 29% against 35-45% guided; operating cash flow was -₹130 Cr in FY26 with working-capital days of 359; Ideal Explosives lags; large orders (MIGM, QRSAM, Pinaka) are not yet placed, and no FY28 numbers have been given.
About 113x earnings and about 57x EV/EBITDA; the illustrative bull case is about 17% above the current market cap.

blocks.text: Apollo Micro Systems, founded in 1985 and led by Karunakar Reddy Baddam, designs and makes defence electronics and subsystems: guidance and onboard computers, fuzes and actuators, power and control electronics and naval systems, mainly for DRDO programmes and prime contractors such as BDL, BEL and MIL. Through acquisitions it has added explosives: Ideal Explosives (a subsidiary) and, pending, Premier Explosives, which the Joint MD says would let it supply a complete missile.

items.text: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹306 Cr (+36%), EBITDA ₹108 Cr (35% margin), PAT ₹48 Cr. About ₹1,300 Cr of the order book.
Commercial explosives subsidiary, loss-making until recently on thin margins; a silo near Asansol was commissioned for Coal India orders. Turnaround 'a couple of quarters more'.
The Competition Commission has cleared the transaction and an open offer to public shareholders follows. Management will not comment on Premier until it closes.
New company with Dr V. K. Saraswat to design long-range weapons; Apollo holds about 33-34% and will manufacture.
MIGM (naval mine; about ₹3,500 Cr budget, Apollo expects about 70%), QRSAM and Akash-NG missile subsystems, Pinaka rocket components, Varunastra and heavyweight torpedoes, moored and limpet mines.
items.src: Aug call p.8; Oct call p.8, 17

items.text: Unit 3 is about 12 times the present facility; its first phase is operating and the whole is due before March 2027.

blocks.title: Net profit vs operating cash flow, ₹ Cr
blocks.caption: Over five years profit was ₹228 Cr and operating cash flow -₹171 Cr, from FY23 onwards: defence stock and receivables are built ahead of delivery.

blocks.note: From the company's Q2 FY27 deck (p.10-14); borrowings/equity computed from its balance sheet. Screener's ROCE is 14.5%.

items.text: Poor so far. Inventory ₹795 Cr and receivables ₹481 Cr at March 2026 against ₹156 Cr of cash; operating cash flow was -₹130 Cr in FY26 and +₹22 Cr in H1 FY27. Management expects steady positive operating cash flow only from FY29.
Borrowings ₹543 Cr at March 2026 (₹335 Cr a year earlier). Equity rose from about ₹608 Cr to ₹1,308 Cr in FY26, far more than profit, which fits a share issue.
₹357 Cr of investing cash outflow in FY26 and ₹196 Cr of work in progress at March; Unit 3 and an in-house test facility are being built.
ROCE 14.5%, ROE 11.8% on Screener's current figures. Our ROIIC was not computed because the Sept balance sheet was not read.

blocks.title: Points to read in the annual report

items.text: Promoters 49.98%, institutions 7.45% and public 42.58% at September 2026 (company deck). Pledges were not checked.
The annual report was not read for this note: auditor remarks, related-party dealings and the Premier and Ideal accounting are still to be checked.
Management declined to comment on Premier under the share purchase agreement and on its program-level order book; a number of programmes are described as strategic and unnamed.
Standalone effective tax rate was about 51% in Q2 because a lower regime no longer applies (CFO).

blocks.note: Screener's figures. Data Patterns and Sigma are the closest listed defence-electronics names; BEL is the scale incumbent and BDL a customer.

items.text: On MIGM the company says it is the only supplier of the electronics; on QRSAM it is sole source on some subsystems and shares others. DRDO policy generally wants two vendors, so second sources can arrive.
Management says new entrants need four to five years to clear quality audits; the Whole-time Director adds that sustaining lumpy business is the real barrier.
MoD is splitting QRSAM 50:50 between BDL and private industry; Pralay is only at RFQ stage; large systems orders have been muted.
Two explosives acquisitions, a weapon-design venture and a large new factory arrive together.

items.text: Revenue ₹2,100 Cr and PAT margin 12.5% (₹262 Cr) valued at 70x: MIGM lands early and Premier adds profit.

items.name: Base
items.text: Revenue ₹1,700 Cr (about +35% on a ₹1,260 Cr FY27) at 11% (₹187 Cr), valued at 60x.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Revenue ₹1,400 Cr at 9% (₹126 Cr), valued at 45x: orders slip and working capital absorbs cash.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative arithmetic on stated assumptions, not company guidance (management has not given FY28 numbers); percentages are against the 6 Nov market cap of ₹15,715 Cr.

At about ₹15,700 Cr the market values Apollo at roughly 13x the last four quarters' revenue (₹1,184 Cr on Screener's rows) and about 57x EBITDA of ₹283 Cr, using March net debt of ₹387 Cr. The price already assumes the MIGM order arrives, margins stay above 25% and the energetics acquisitions pay off, while operating cash flow has been negative. This is a note on valuation, not a buy or sell call.
